title: Assessment of the Binding Patterns for Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals in Complex with Estrogen and Androgen Receptors by Leveraging the Asclepios Enalos KNIME Nodes.
authors: Tzoupis, Haralampos; Papadourakis, Michail; Papavasileiou, Konstantinos D; Burk, Oliver; Lauschke, Volker M; Tsoumanis, Andreas; Melagraki, Georgia; Afantitis, Antreas
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用MM-GBSA和相对结合自由能计算评估内分泌干扰物与雌激素/雄激素受体的结合模式，属于广义蛋白-配体互作，非TF-DNA体系，但物理模拟方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA结合建模。
abstract: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) have been shown to mediate metabolic disruptions in human cells and have been associated with severe adverse health effects. By antagonizing the hormones that act on nuclear hormone receptors, like the estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha) and the androgen receptor (AR), these chemicals disrupt the regulation of various biochemical processes, thereby adversely affecting metabolic homeostasis. The expression of estrogen and androgen receptors in the liver and pancreas, which play an important role in lipid and glucose homeostasis regulation, has made them prime targets affected by EDCs. The different chemical structures of EDCs impose limitations on elucidating their binding mechanisms in nuclear receptors. In this context, in silico tools are able to highlight the potential interactions between the chemicals and the receptors. The aim of this study is to apply molecular simulation and experimental techniques to identify common patterns in the binding process of selected EDCs to ERalpha and AR and, thus, pinpoint key elements that could be characterized as molecular initiating events (MIE). MM-GBSA and alchemical relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations have verified the trends observed in the experimental assays regarding the binding affinity of bisphenol compounds. The findings that confirm the agreement between computational and experimental methods offer a framework for future studies on the behavior of EDCs with other metabolically relevant receptors.
abstract_zh: 内分泌干扰化学物质（EDCs）已被证明可介导人类细胞中的代谢紊乱，并与严重的不良健康效应相关联。通过拮抗作用于核激素受体（如雌激素受体α（ERalpha）和雄激素受体（AR））的激素，这些化学物质干扰了多种生化过程的调控，从而对代谢稳态产生不利影响。雌激素和雄激素受体在肝脏和胰腺中的表达，这些器官在脂质和葡萄糖稳态调节中发挥重要作用，使其成为EDCs影响的主要靶点。EDCs的不同化学结构限制了阐明其在核受体中结合机制的可行性。在此背景下，计算机模拟工具能够突出化学物质与受体之间的潜在相互作用。本研究旨在应用分子模拟和实验技术，识别选定的EDCs与ERalpha和AR结合过程中的共同模式，从而确定可表征为分子起始事件（MIE）的关键要素。MM-GBSA和热力学积分相对结合自由能（RBFE）计算验证了实验测定中关于双酚化合物结合亲和力的趋势。确认计算与实验方法一致性的发现，为未来研究EDCs与其他代谢相关受体的行为提供了框架。
